newsitem.title: USA: Clinton vows veto of disaster aid bill.
newsitem.headline: Clinton vows veto of disaster aid bill.

text.p: President Clinton Wednesday night vowed to veto a compromise disaster aid bill for more than 30 states that was reached by congressional negotiators, calling it "flawed legislation."

"If the Republican majority is set on this course of adding contentious and extraneous provisions, they should send this bill as quickly as possible," Clinton said in a statement. "I will veto it as soon as it arrives."

House and Senate negotiators Wednesday approved legislation to provide emergency relief to disaster-stricken states, but insisted on keeping Republican-backed conditions that Clinton has called unacceptable.
Clinton said he will return the bill to Congress swiftly "so they can send me a clean disaster assistance bill immediately that keeps aid flowing to those in need."
"Americans in need should not have to endure this unnecessary delay," he said.

Clinton objects to language in the bill that would prevent a government shut-down in case of another budget impasse between Congress and the White House. He also opposes a section that would dictate how the government conducts the 2000 census.

The White House contends the government shut-down provision would remove incentives for Congress to negotiate on the budget, and claims Republican changes in census procedures would under estimate minorities and poor people.
